messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the autoscale policy tweak this morning, grafana -> fleet/queue-headroom is super spiky for eu-west. Alerts fired a few times. p95 queue_wait increased for some models.
kevin: Can you paste the panel PromQL and a screenshot?
maria: Putting the query we use for the headroom panel:
```
# headroom-ish metric (simplified)
sum(rate(redwood_queue_depth_seconds_count{region="eu-west"}[1m])) by (pool)
/
sum(redwood_gpu_capacity{region="eu-west"}) by (pool)
```
maria: Also the p95 wait we graph: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_queue_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
```
maria: Short version: small bursts blow up queue_depth briefly, autoscaler reacts, then headroom swings. Alerts are noisy.
devon: ops-bot pasted the scale events into the thread: 
ops-bot: [scale-event] 2026-03-17T08:12:34Z eu-west pool-gpu resized +4 -> triggered by queue_depth > threshold
ops-bot: [scale-event] 2026-03-17T08:13:05Z eu-west pool-gpu resized -2 -> cooldown
kevin: The rapid up/down probably causes the headroom panel to look worse than user impact. We should 1) debounce alerts 2) annotate scale events on the dashboard 3) surface effective_batch_size and inflight_batches in the same panel to see correlation.
tara: Agreed. Current alert rule is `queue_headroom_critical` with `for: 30s` and threshold 0.15. That's too tight for short spikes. Proposal: for eu-west pools set `for: 5m` for paging alerts and keep a `for: 1m` slack-only warning. Add a separate noise-floor alert that ignores bursts < 20% of capacity.
kevin: +1. Also add an annotation query to overlay `redwood_autoscale_events_total` so graph shows exact scale-up/down timestamps.
devon: Cost note: since the autoscale change our eu GPU spend is up ~12% month-over-month (rough calc). If we extend the hold period we might save churn + cost. I'll add a cost annotation panel.
maria: For instrumentation, can we emit `effective_batch_size{model, pool}` and `inflight_batches{pool}`? That would help decide if bursts are amplified by small batches.
tara: Yes, runtime team agreed to emit `effective_batch_size` last sprint — I can prod them to enable labels for pool and model.
kevin: For alert tuning, suggested thresholds:
- queue_headroom_warning: headroom < 0.2 for 1m (slack)
- queue_headroom_pager: headroom < 0.12 for 5m (pager)
- queue_wait_p95_warning: p95 > 200ms for 2m (slack)
- queue_wait_p95_pager: p95 > 500ms for 5m (pager)
kevin: Also add runbook link in alert -> /runbooks/autoscale-oscillation.md and a note to check `effective_batch_size`.
ops-bot: [alert] queue_headroom_warning eu-west pool-gpu fired at 2026-03-17T08:12:58Z -> suppressed by cooldown rule
devon: I'll create a new grafana panel that overlays queue_depth, p95_wait, effective_batch_size and autoscale events. Will also add a small table with recent scale events.
maria: Can you also add a short-term dashboard for on-call: single-screen with 3 panels: headroom trend (30m), inflight_batches + batch size, and scale event timeline.
devon: Yep. Target PR today, dashboard id will be `fleet-ops/eu-headroom-ops` and I'll tag the changes for review.
tara: For SLOs we should add a synthetic: queue_wait_p95 per model < 200ms, objective 99% monthly. If that is breached, auto-create eval ticket to check model-specific batch config.
kevin: One more: add a prom recording rule `fleet:queue_headroom:avg5m` to smooth spikes for alerting vs raw panel.
maria: Sounds good. Thanks all. I'll update the incident notes and mark this as "monitoring improvement" for the sprint. :thumbsup:
tara: Thanks — will update alert rules in the staging prometheus and smoke test with load generator. :eyes:
kevin: ping @oncall when PRs merged so we can observe next rollout behavior.
ops-bot: [info] dashboard `fleet-ops/eu-headroom-ops` created draft by devon
maria: Ack, closing thread for now. If anyone sees pager noise after the changes, re-open. :rotating_light:
